artifact: Merged P2 preflight completion report projections

overall.one_line_summary: The P2 preflight implementation and read model remain valid, but a clean Windows checkout fails the required full report byte check for internal generated projections.
strengths: The read model, P2 lifecycle state, proposal validation, focused tests, safety policies, and merged CI remained valid.
The drift was confined to generated projection line endings and did not alter scientific state or protected data.
weaknesses: The full report check reported 17 internal projection paths as drifted after Git converted LF renderer output to CRLF on Windows checkout.
The existing CI used read-model-only drift validation and had no checked-in regression that compared all internal generated projection bytes.

strengths: The full report checker directly exposed the checkout-specific mismatch.
weaknesses: CI evidence covered read-model equality but not the affected full internal report byte set.
suggestions: Add a checkout-stability assertion for every internal output rendered by projection_report_contents.

strengths: The failure is reproducible with myis-report check on a clean Windows checkout.
weaknesses: No test encoded the exact LF byte policy for the three affected generated-output roots.
suggestions: Bind the affected paths in .gitattributes and assert the entries in tests.

strengths: The finding is limited to reporting reproducibility and makes no measured P2 claim.
Text-normalized content matched the deterministic renderer.
weaknesses: The merged closeout claimed report checks passed while the authoritative full check failed on the current clean Windows checkout.
suggestions: Repair raw-byte checkout policy and rerun the full check twice before closeout.

strengths: The completion audit retained the contradictory failure instead of accepting the green read-model-only CI result.
weaknesses: The failure was discovered only after merge because local pre-merge files had not been rewritten by checkout.
suggestions: Exercise a checkout-stable byte assertion in the normal full test suite.

strengths: The report renderer is deterministic and already compares exact bytes.
weaknesses: Generated MLflow, compatibility, and phase/task report paths lacked an explicit no-normalization policy.
suggestions: Preserve LF bytes for the affected roots and regenerate through one validated read-model object.

findings.evidence_locator: myis-report check reported report_drift for mlflow/generated/archive-index.v2.json, projections/obsidian/generated/program-status.md, and 15 projections/reports JSON files
findings.observation: Git checkout converted deterministic LF output to CRLF because the affected generated roots had no explicit byte-preservation attributes.
findings.reasoning: The required full report check fails on the current clean Windows checkout, so cross-platform completion is not proven even though parsed content and read-model-only CI pass.
findings.suggestion: Add -text attributes for the affected generated roots, regenerate from one read model, and add a raw-byte regression over all internal projection outputs.

findings.target_entity: Validate active layout and projections step
findings.evidence_locator: The workflow runs myis-report check --read-model-only and relies on the full pytest suite for repository-local contracts.
findings.observation: The full suite had no regression that checked raw bytes for all repository-local generated projections.
findings.reasoning: A green CI run did not falsify the Windows-only byte drift.
findings.suggestion: Add a platform-independent internal projection byte test to the full pytest suite while retaining local full report checks for sibling projections.

questions_for_owner: No new Owner scientific or gate decision is required for this reporting-byte repair.
